target_audience: Advanced high school students or first-year university students

sections.title: The Bridge: Discrete vs. Continuous
lecture_lines: Discrete events involve counting specific individual points.
Continuous events involve measuring values within a range.
Like measuring a cat's jump distance precisely.
animations: Show a rolling die landing on 4. [Color die #ADD8E6]
Show a ruler measuring a jump distance. [Color marker #FFD700]
Ruler turns into a smooth line segment. [Color line #FFFFFF]

sections.title: The Evolution: From Histogram to Curve
lecture_lines: Histograms show data frequency using discrete bars.
Narrower bins create a smoother silhouette of data.
Infinitely thin bins reveal the continuous PDF curve.
animations: Show 12-bar histogram of rainfall data. [Color bars #87CEFA]
Increase to 365 thin bars. [Color bars #00BFFF]
Smooth curve appears, bars fade away. [Color curve #FFFFFF]

sections.title: The Core Concept: Height vs. Area
lecture_lines: Curve height represents density, not exact probability.
Density shows where data points cluster most thickly.
Probability is the area under the curve between points.
Sand depth shows density; volume shows the probability.
We measure ranges, never just a single exact point.
animations: Draw a smooth curve with height f(x). [Color curve #90EE90]
Point height flashes; probability at a point is zero. [Color #FF0000]
Define an interval [a, b] on x-axis. [Color x-axis #FFFFFF]
Shade area between a and b under curve. [Color #FFFFE0]
Label shaded area as "Probability = Area". [Color label #FFFFFF]

sections.title: The Two Golden Rules
lecture_lines: A PDF must never fall below the horizontal axis.
Negative probability is impossible in the real world.
The total area under the curve must equal one.
One represents a one-hundred percent chance of any outcome.
The "Magic Carpet" always covers exactly one unit.
animations: Show a curve strictly above the x-axis. [Color curve #FFB6C1]
Display a "No Negative" symbol below the x-axis then cross it out. [Color #FF0000]
Shade the entire area under the curve from start to end. [Color #E6E6FA]
Display "100%" label that transforms into a large "1". [Color label #FFFFFF]
Show the entire shaded area (the "Magic Carpet") glow intensely. [Color glow #FFFF00]

sections.title: Application: The Arrival Window
lecture_lines: Imagine Zippy the drone delivering your package today.
The curve shows likely arrival times around ten-thirty.
Shading the region from ten-twenty-five to ten-thirty-five.
This area represents the chance of an on-time delivery.
Calculus helps us calculate this specific shaded area.
animations: Show the drone asset [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg] [Color #87CEEB] hovering above a timeline.
Draw a bell curve centered at a "10:30" marker. [Color curve #AFEEEE]
Shade the region between "10:25" and "10:35" markers. [Color #FFFACD]
The shaded region pulses and displays the text "P(Arrival)". [Color #FFFFFF]
An integration symbol (integral) slides over the shaded area. [Color symbol #FFD700]

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaway
lecture_lines: PDFs map the likelihood landscape of continuous variables.
Remember the golden rule: Area always equals probability.
This tool unlocks understanding of our continuous world.
animations: Display various glowing PDF shapes. [Color curves #D3D3D3]
Highlight a slice; "Area = Probability" glows. [Color glow #FFFF00]
Text "Mapping the Likelihood Landscape" fades in alongside the map icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg]. [Color text #FFFFFF]
